1252:    /// @dev Computes the price and transfers winnings.
1253:    /// Does NOT transfer ownership of token.
1254:    function _bid(uint256 _tokenId, uint256 _bidAmount)
1255:        internal
1256:        returns (uint256)
1257:    {
1258:        // Get a reference to the auction struct
1259:        Auction storage auction = tokenIdToAuction[_tokenId];
1260:
1261:        // Explicitly check that this auction is currently live.
1262:        // (Because of how Ethereum mappings work, we can't just count
1263:        // on the lookup above failing. An invalid _tokenId will just
1264:        // return an auction object that is all zeros.)
1265:        require(_isOnAuction(auction));
1266:
1267:        // Check that the bid is greater than or equal to the current price
1268:        uint256 price = _currentPrice(auction);
1269:        require(_bidAmount >= price);
1270:
1271:        // Grab a reference to the seller before the auction struct
1272:        // gets deleted.
1273:        address seller = auction.seller;
1274:
1275:        // The bid is good! Remove the auction before sending the fees
1276:        // to the sender so we can't have a reentrancy attack.
1277:        _removeAuction(_tokenId);
1278:
1279:        // Transfer proceeds to seller (if there are any!)
1280:        if (price > 0) {
1281:            // Calculate the auctioneer's cut.
1282:            // (NOTE: _computeCut() is guaranteed to return a
1283:            // value <= price, so this subtraction can't go negative.)
1284:            uint256 auctioneerCut = _computeCut(price);
1285:            uint256 sellerProceeds = price - auctioneerCut;
1286:
1287:            // NOTE: Doing a transfer() in the middle of a complex
1288:            // method like this is generally discouraged because of
1289:            // reentrancy attacks and DoS attacks if the seller is
1290:            // a contract with an invalid fallback function. We explicitly
1291:            // guard against reentrancy attacks by removing the auction
1292:            // before calling transfer(), and the only thing the seller
1293:            // can DoS is the sale of their own asset! (And if it's an
1294:            // accident, they can call cancelAuction(). )
1295:            seller.transfer(sellerProceeds);
1296:        }
1297:
1298:        // Calculate any excess funds included with the bid. If the excess
1299:        // is anything worth worrying about, transfer it back to bidder.
1300:        // NOTE: We checked above that the bid amount is greater than or
1301:        // equal to the price so this cannot underflow.
1302:        uint256 bidExcess = _bidAmount - price;
1303:
1304:        // Return the funds. Similar to the previous transfer, this is
1305:        // not susceptible to a re-entry attack because the auction is
1306:        // removed before any transfers occur.
1307:        msg.sender.transfer(bidExcess);
1308:
1309:        // Tell the world!
1310:        AuctionSuccessful(_tokenId, price, msg.sender);
1311:
1312:        return price;
1313:    }

1252:    /// @dev Computes the price and transfers winnings.
1253:    /// Does NOT transfer ownership of token.
1254:    function _bid(uint256 _tokenId, uint256 _bidAmount)
1255:        internal
1256:        returns (uint256)
1257:    {
1258:        // Get a reference to the auction struct
1259:        Auction storage auction = tokenIdToAuction[_tokenId];
1260:
1261:        // Explicitly check that this auction is currently live.
1262:        // (Because of how Ethereum mappings work, we can't just count
1263:        // on the lookup above failing. An invalid _tokenId will just
1264:        // return an auction object that is all zeros.)
1265:        require(_isOnAuction(auction));
1266:
1267:        // Check that the bid is greater than or equal to the current price
1268:        uint256 price = _currentPrice(auction);
1269:        require(_bidAmount >= price);
1270:
1271:        // Grab a reference to the seller before the auction struct
1272:        // gets deleted.
1273:        address seller = auction.seller;
1274:
1275:        // The bid is good! Remove the auction before sending the fees
1276:        // to the sender so we can't have a reentrancy attack.
1277:        _removeAuction(_tokenId);
1278:
1279:        // Transfer proceeds to seller (if there are any!)
1280:        if (price > 0) {
1281:            // Calculate the auctioneer's cut.
1282:            // (NOTE: _computeCut() is guaranteed to return a
1283:            // value <= price, so this subtraction can't go negative.)
1284:            uint256 auctioneerCut = _computeCut(price);
1285:            uint256 sellerProceeds = price - auctioneerCut;
1286:
1287:            // NOTE: Doing a transfer() in the middle of a complex
1288:            // method like this is generally discouraged because of
1289:            // reentrancy attacks and DoS attacks if the seller is
1290:            // a contract with an invalid fallback function. We explicitly
1291:            // guard against reentrancy attacks by removing the auction
1292:            // before calling transfer(), and the only thing the seller
1293:            // can DoS is the sale of their own asset! (And if it's an
1294:            // accident, they can call cancelAuction(). )
1295:            seller.transfer(sellerProceeds);
1296:        }
1297:
1298:        // Calculate any excess funds included with the bid. If the excess
1299:        // is anything worth worrying about, transfer it back to bidder.
1300:        // NOTE: We checked above that the bid amount is greater than or
1301:        // equal to the price so this cannot underflow.
1302:        uint256 bidExcess = _bidAmount - price;
1303:
1304:        // Return the funds. Similar to the previous transfer, this is
1305:        // not susceptible to a re-entry attack because the auction is
1306:        // removed before any transfers occur.
1307:        msg.sender.transfer(bidExcess);
1308:
1309:        // Tell the world!
1310:        AuctionSuccessful(_tokenId, price, msg.sender);
1311:
1312:        return price;
1313:    }
